words.gloss: siddhabasti (a named enema, lit. 'proven enema'); preparation (kalpa)

hindi: अब इसलिए हम सिद्धबस्ति-कल्प की व्याख्या करेंगे।
english: Now, therefore, we shall explain the preparations of the siddhabasti (a named enema; lit. 'proven enema').
notes: Chapter-opening formula. Printed 'athātaḥ' is read atha + ataḥ with the visarga kept. basti = enema (vasti normalised to basti).

hindi: सिद्धबस्तियों का सब देहधारियों के लिए सदा प्रयोग करे।
english: One should always employ siddhabastis (the named enemas) for all embodied beings.
notes: Genitive 'sarvadehinām' is rendered 'for all embodied beings'; a literal alternative is 'of all embodied beings'.

words.gram: m. nom. sg. (as printed); agreement uncertain
tat-puruṣa, first members of a compound ending in karān in the next token

hindi: ये बिना विपत्ति के, बहुत फल देने वाले, बल और बुद्धि बढ़ाने वाले तथा सुखद हैं।
english: (They are) free from mishap, of many benefits, producing strength and intelligence, and pleasant.

text_flags.why: possible: v for b (n+b is regularly written nb); 'bala' (strength) fits the sense
possible: the other adjectives are accusative plural and agree with the siddhabastis of 2; 'nirvyāpadaḥ' (nominative singular) does not agree

notes: Continues 2 (adjectives of the siddhabastis). The compound 'bala-buddhi-karān' runs across the token break. The Hindi and English supply 'they are' only as the copula the construction needs; the text has no verb.

words.gloss: miśi (dill, Anethum sowa; disputed: fennel, Foeniculum vulgare, also given)

hindi: मधु और तैल बराबर; एक कर्ष; सैन्धव से दो पिचु; मिशि।
english: Honey and oil, equal; one karṣa (a unit of weight); from rock salt (saindhava), two picu (a unit of weight); miśi (dill).
notes: Elliptic list of quantities with no verb; the exact relation of 'karṣaḥ' and 'saindhavāt dvipicuḥ' to the ingredients is not clear from the line (commentarial reading: one karṣa of rock salt, two picu of miśi; not applied here). Identifications: saindhava = rock salt (standard); miśi = dill, Anethum sowa (disputed; fennel also proposed).

words.gloss: castor (eraṇḍa, Ricinus communis; standard); root; decoction

hindi: एरण्ड यानी अरंडी की जड़ के काढ़े से मधु और तैल वाला निरूह यानी काढ़े की बस्ति।
english: The nirūha (decoction enema) made with a decoction of the root of eraṇḍa (castor), with honey and oil.

text_flags.why: possible: 'kāthena' lacks the v of kvātha (decoction); sense and parallels in the chapter point to kvātha

notes: No verb in the line; it names the enema. Identification: eraṇḍa = Ricinus communis (standard).

words.gloss: prameha (a group of urinary disorders, linked with diabetes; probable); arśas (haemorrhoids, piles; standard)
words.gram: dvandva, first members of the compound

words.gloss: worms; gulma (abdominal lump); intestine; enlargement; dispelling
words.gram: tat-puruṣa, m. nom. sg.; antravṛddhi = intestinal hernia (standard)

hindi: यह रसायन है, तथा प्रमेह यानी मूत्र-विकार, अर्श यानी बवासीर, कृमि यानी कीड़े, गुल्म यानी पेट की गाँठ और अन्त्रवृद्धि यानी आँत उतरना या हर्निया को दूर करने वाला है।
english: It is rejuvenating (rasāyana) and dispels prameha (a group of urinary disorders), arśas (haemorrhoids), worms, gulma (abdominal lump) and antravṛddhi (intestinal hernia).
notes: Continues 5; the adjectives agree with nirūhaḥ. 'pramehārśaḥ' read as prameha-arśaḥ (sandhi a+a). Identifications: arśas = haemorrhoids (standard); prameha = urinary disorders, commonly linked with diabetes (probable); antravṛddhi = hernia (standard).

words.gram: tat-puruṣa, m. nom. sg.; raktapitta = bleeding from upper or lower passages (probable)

hindi: और यष्टीमधु यानी मुलेठी के साथ, आँखों के लिए हितकर तथा रक्तपित्त को जीतने वाला।
english: And with licorice (yaṣṭīmadhu), good for the eyes, conquering raktapitta (a bleeding disorder).
notes: Continues 5-6 (the nirūha with licorice added). Identification: yaṣṭīmadhu = Glycyrrhiza glabra (standard); raktapitta = a bleeding disorder, lit. 'blood-pitta' (probable).

words.gram: bahuvrīhi, m. nom. sg.; ājya = ghee

hindi: यापन, गाढ़े कल्क से युक्त तथा मधु, तैल, वसा यानी चर्बी और घी वाला।
english: The yāpana (sustaining enema), with a thick paste, and having honey, oil, fat (vasā) and ghee.
notes: No verb. 'ghana-kalka' = thick paste of drugs. 'madhutailavasājyavān' read as madhu-taila-vasā-ājya + vat (having).

words.gloss: anus; knee; thigh; pṛṣṭaśaṇa (unclear: printed form, probably pṛṣṭha 'back' + śroṇi 'hip' on a conjectural reading); bladder region; penis (mehana)
words.gram: tat-puruṣa, first members of a compound ending in śūlajit

hindi: यह गुदा, घुटने, जाँघ, पीठ और कूल्हे (एक अस्पष्ट शब्द पर अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार), मूत्राशय और लिंग की पीड़ा को जीतने वाला है।
english: It conquers pain in the anus, knee, thigh, back and hip (on a conjectural reading of the damaged word), bladder region and penis (mehana).

text_flags.why: possible: 'pṛṣṭaśaṇa' is not a word; 'pṛṣṭha-śroṇi' (back, hip) fits a list of body parts; the final -a of mehana before śūlajit is also doubtful (mehana-śūlajit)

notes: The compound 'pāyu...mehana-śūlajit' is read as 'conquering pain of anus, knee, ... penis'. The middle of the compound is doubtful, so the translation of 'back and hip' is conjectural. Continues 8.

hindi: प्रसृत के भागों से, घी, शहद, वसा यानी चर्बी और तैल के साथ तैयार करे।
english: One should prepare, with portions of one prasṛta (a handful measure) each, with ghee, honey, fat (vasā) and oil.
notes: Instrumental plural of the four substances; 'prasṛta' is a measure (about two palas in the standard tables).

words.gloss: rock salt (saindhava); half; akṣa (a unit of weight)
hapuṣā (juniper berries, Juniperus communis; probable); half; pala (a unit of weight)

hindi: यापन, आधे अक्ष सैन्धव और आधे पल हपुषा यानी सम्भवतः हाऊबेर से युक्त।
english: The yāpana (sustaining enema), accompanied by half an akṣa (a unit of weight) of rock salt (saindhava) and half a pala (a unit of weight) of hapuṣā (probably juniper berries).
notes: Printed 'arddha' normalised to ardha (doubled dd). The division of the compound into 'half akṣa of saindhava' and 'half pala of hapuṣā' is the natural reading but the line has no separating word. hapuṣā = Juniperus communis (probable).

hindi: एरण्ड की जड़ का काढ़ा, शहद, तैल, सैन्धव के साथ।
english: A decoction of the root of eraṇḍa (castor), honey, oil, with rock salt (saindhava).

text_flags.why: possible: 'niḥkkātha' for niḥkvātha (decoction); the doubled k and missing v are probably print errors

notes: A list of ingredients with no verb; it continues the description of the yāpana of 11.

words.gloss: with vacā (sweet flag, Acorus calamus; standard); pippalī (long pepper, Piper longum; standard)

hindi: यह युक्तरथ बस्ति है, वचा यानी बच, पिप्पली यानी पीपर और फल के साथ।
english: This is the yuktaratha enema (basti), with vacā (sweet flag), pippalī (long pepper) and fruit (phala).
notes: 'savacāpippalī phalaḥ' is read sa-vacā-pippalī-phalaḥ; the fruit (phala) is not named further and might also be read as 'pippalī fruit'. The printed space after 'savacāpippalī' is kept in src. Identifications: vacā = Acorus calamus (standard); pippalī = Piper longum (standard).

hindi: काढ़े के साथ, शहद, एक अस्पष्ट शब्द (छपा रूप पैण्डुण्ठा) पर अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार, शताह्वा यानी सम्भवतः सोया, हींग और सैन्धव।
english: With a decoction, honey, paiṃḍhuṃthā (on a conjectural reading; the printed word is unclear), śatāhvā (probably dill), asafoetida (hiṅgu) and rock salt (saindhava).

text_flags.why: possible: letters transposed; śatāhvā is the usual word
the printed word is not a known drug name; possibly a name beginning pi- (e.g. a corrupt form of a drug name), kept unsplit and unglossed

notes: List of ingredients with no verb. 'paiṃḍhuṃthā' is damaged or corrupt in print and is not interpreted. śatāhvā = Anethum sowa, dill (probable; fennel also proposed).

words.gloss: suradāru (devadāru, Himalayan cedar, Cedrus deodara; standard)
rāsnā (probably Pluchea lanceolata; disputed, Alpinia galanga also given)

hindi: सुरदारु यानी देवदार और रास्ना, जिसकी पहचान में मतभेद है; यह बस्ति के दोषों को हरने वाला और कल्याणकारी है।
english: Suradāru (devadāru, deodar cedar) and rāsnā (probably Pluchea lanceolata), removing the faults of the enema (basti-doṣa), auspicious.
notes: 'bastidoṣa' is read as faults (defects or ill effects) of the enema. The line continues the list begun in 12-14; the adjectives apply to the whole preparation. Identifications: suradāru = Cedrus deodara (standard); rāsnā = Pluchea lanceolata (disputed; Alpinia galanga also proposed).

words.gloss: five; roots; pañcamūla (a group of five roots; which group is not stated)
māgadhikā (long pepper, Piper longum; standard synonym of pippalī)

hindi: पंचमूल का काढ़ा, तैल, मागधिका यानी पिप्पली और शहद।
english: A decoction of the pañcamūla (the group of five roots), oil, māgadhikā (long pepper) and honey.

text_flags.why: possible: 'niḥkkātha' for niḥkvātha (decoction); the visarga + t- sandhi (niḥkvāthaḥ + tailam -> niḥkvāthastailam) is regular

notes: Ingredient list with no verb. Which pañcamūla (the lesser or the greater five) is not stated here.

hindi: सैन्धव और मधुक सहित यह सिद्धबस्ति कहा गया है।
english: With rock salt (saindhava) and madhuka (probably licorice), it is called the siddhabasti.
notes: 'samadhukaḥ' could also be read sa-madhu-kaḥ ('with honey'), but honey is already named in 16, so madhuka (licorice, probable) is taken.

words.gloss: two; pañcamūla (double five-root group, i.e. ten roots)

hindi: द्विपंचमूल, त्रिफला, फल और बिल्व को पकाए।
english: One should cook the dvipañcamūla (the double five-root group, ten roots), triphalā (the three fruits), fruit (phala) and bilva (bael).
notes: Printed 'vilva' normalised to bilva. The compound is read as a list of four; 'phala' is not specified and may belong to the preceding word. bilva = Aegle marmelos (standard). Continues in 19.

words.gloss: pāṭhā (probably Cissampelos pareira; probable); vatsaka (kuṭaja, Holarrhena antidysenterica; probable); toyada (musta, Cyperus rotundus; probable; lit. 'water-giver')

hindi: गोमूत्र में, उससे, तथा पाठा, वत्सक और तोयद के पिसे हुए के साथ।
english: In cow's urine, by that, and with the ground (ones) of pāṭhā (probably Cissampelos pareira), vatsaka (probably kuṭaja) and toyada (probably musta).

text_flags.why: possible: 'tenai' is not a form; 'tena' (by that) fits sense and metre

notes: Continues 18 (verb pācayet carried over); no verb in this line. Identifications: pāṭhā = Cissampelos pareira (probable); vatsaka = Holarrhena antidysenterica, kuṭaja (probable); toyada = Cyperus rotundus, musta (probable).

hindi: फलों सहित, शहद और तैल दोनों से, क्षार से और लवण से भी।
english: With fruits, with honey and oil (both), with kṣāra and with salt (lavaṇa).
notes: Printed 'ḻ' in saphaḻaiḥ is read as ordinary l (print variant). Continues 18-19 (instrumentals of added substances); no verb here.

words.gloss: pāṇḍu (pale); disease; the disease pāṇḍu, anaemia with pallor (standard)
visūcī (acute vomiting and purging, cholera-like illness; probable)

hindi: यह बस्ति कफ-व्याधियों में, पाण्डु-रोग यानी फीकेपन वाली रक्ताल्पता में और विसूची यानी उलटी-दस्त वाली तीव्र बीमारी में उपयुक्त है।
english: The enema (basti) is suitable in Kapha disorders, in pāṇḍu disease (anaemia with pallor) and in visūcī (acute vomiting and purging, a cholera-like illness).
notes: The sentence continues in 22. 'yuktaḥ' is taken as 'suitable' (literally 'joined, applied'). Identifications: pāṇḍuroga = anaemia with pallor (standard); visūcī = acute vomiting and purging, cholera-like (probable). 'kaphavyādhi' read as a disorder of Kapha.

hindi: शुक्र और अनिल यानी वायु की रुकावटों में तथा बस्ति के आटोप यानी गुड़गुड़ाहट वाले फूलाव में यह प्रशंसित है।
english: In obstructions of semen and of wind (anila), and in āṭopa (rumbling distension) of the bladder region (basti), it is esteemed.
notes: Continues 21. 'basti' in 'bastyāṭopa' is read as the bladder region, not the enema; 'āṭopa' = rumbling or distension (probable). 'anila' (wind) is the wind-humour or simply wind; kept as 'wind'.

words.gloss: amṛtā (guḍūcī, Tinospora cordifolia; standard); the printed word is broken across the token break
(completes amṛta; sandhi a+e gives ai in -mṛtairaṇḍa)

hindi: मुस्ता, पाठा, अमृता यानी गिलोय, एरण्ड, बला यानी सम्भवतः बरियार, रास्ना और पुनर्नवा।
english: Musta (nut-grass), pāṭhā, amṛtā (guḍūcī, Tinospora cordifolia), eraṇḍa (castor), balā (probably Sida cordifolia), rāsnā and punarnavā (Boerhavia diffusa).

text_flags.why: possible: the printed space falls inside amṛta+eraṇḍa (amṛtairaṇḍa); the two tokens form one word

notes: A list with no verb; the drugs go with the preparation of 24-27. The token break inside 'amṛtairaṇḍa' is a print artefact. Identifications: musta = Cyperus rotundus (standard); amṛtā = Tinospora cordifolia (standard); balā = Sida cordifolia (probable); punarnavā = Boerhavia diffusa (standard); pāṭhā and rāsnā as in 19 and 15.

words.gloss: rohiṇī (unclear which drug: kaṭukā or harītakī; disputed)

hindi: मंजिष्ठा, आरग्वध, उशीर, त्रायमाणा जिसकी पहचान में मतभेद है, अक्ष यानी सम्भवतः बहेड़ा और रोहिणी जिसकी पहचान अस्पष्ट है।
english: Mañjiṣṭhā (Indian madder), āragvadha (Indian laburnum), uśīra (vetiver), trāyamāṇā (identity disputed), akṣa (probably bibhītaka) and rohiṇī (which drug is meant is unclear).
notes: A list with no verb. The reading 'akṣa' + 'rohiṇī' is conjectural; the end of the line could also be one word. Identifications: mañjiṣṭhā = Rubia cordifolia (standard); āragvadha = Cassia fistula (standard); uśīra = Vetiveria zizanioides (standard); trāyamāṇā = disputed (Gentiana kurroo often given); akṣa = Terminalia bellirica (probable); rohiṇī = disputed (kaṭukā, kutki, or harītakī).

words.gloss: of the weight of a pala
madana (emetic nut, Randia dumetorum; probable); set of eight

hindi: छोटा पंचमूल, एक पल के मान का, और आठ मदन।
english: The lesser (kanīyaḥ) pañcamūla (group of five roots), of the weight of one pala each, and eight madana (probably emetic nut, Randia dumetorum).
notes: 'kanīyaḥ pañcamūla' is the lesser five-root group (laghu pañcamūla); its members are not listed in the text. 'pālikam' ('of a pala') may apply to the pañcamūla alone or to all ingredients. madana = Randia dumetorum (probable). Continues 23-24.

hindi: जल के एक आढक में उसे पकाए, चौथाई शेष रहने तक, और छाने।
english: One should cook that in an āḍhaka (a measure of volume) of water, with a quarter remaining, strained.
notes: 'parisrutam' (literally 'flowed through') is read as 'strained'. Continues 23-25.

words.gloss: milk; two; prastha (a measure of volume); joined with

hindi: दो प्रस्थ दूध से युक्त उसे फिर पकाए, जब तक दूध शेष रहे।
english: Joined with two prasthas (a measure of volume) of milk, one should cook it again until the milk remains.
notes: 'kṣīraśeṣam' read as 'until the milk alone remains' (the water having boiled away). The pronoun 'it' stands for the strained decoction of 26.

words.gloss: with a quarter in addition, i.e. one and a quarter (what is measured is not stated)

hindi: सपाद यानी एक और चौथाई जाङ्गल-रस के साथ, घी, शहद और सैन्धव सहित।
english: With jāṅgala-rasa (the juice of dry-land animals) in the amount sapāda (one and a quarter), and with ghee, honey and rock salt (saindhava).
notes: 'sapāda' is 'one and a quarter'; the unit it counts is not stated in this line. 'jāṅgala' is read as 'of dry-land animals'; the line does not say meat. Continues 27.

words.gloss: śyāmā (disputed; black turpeth is often given)
kara (unclear: not a known drug name; possibly karañja, conjectural)
with añjana (collyrium; the substance is not specified)

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार, पिसे हुए यष्टी, मिशि, श्यामा जिसकी पहचान में मतभेद है, कलिङ्ग, कर जो अस्पष्ट शब्द है और अञ्जन के साथ।
english: With the ground (ones): yaṣṭī (licorice), miśi (dill), śyāmā (identity disputed), kaliṅga (probably kuṭaja seed), kara (an unclear word, on a conjectural reading) and añjana (collyrium).

text_flags.why: possible: 'kara' is not a drug name; karañja is a plausible drug in a list with kaliṅga, but this is a guess

notes: List with no verb; continues 26-28. 'kara' is unclear, so the compound is only partly firm. Identifications: yaṣṭī = licorice (standard, as in 7); miśi = dill (disputed, as in 4); śyāmā = disputed; kaliṅga = indrayava or kuṭaja seed (probable).

words.gloss: flesh (muscle); digestive fire (agni); strength; semen; increasing

hindi: यह बस्ति सुखद गर्म है और मांस, अग्नि, बल और शुक्र को बढ़ाने वाली है।
english: The enema (basti), pleasantly warm, increases flesh, the digestive fire (agni), strength and semen.
notes: Printed 'vivarddhanaḥ' normalised to vivardhanaḥ (doubled dh). The 'is' is the copula the construction needs; the text has none. 'sukhoṣṇa' = comfortably warm.

words.gloss: wind; blood; vātāsṛk (wind-blood disorder, gout; probable)

hindi: वातास्र यानी वातरक्त, मेह यानी मूत्र-विकार, मेदस् यानी चर्बी, अर्श यानी बवासीर, गुल्म यानी पेट की गाँठ तथा मल और मूत्र का रुकना।
english: Vātāsṛk (wind-blood disorder, probably gout), meha (urinary disorder), fat (medas), arśas (haemorrhoids), gulma (abdominal lump) and retention of stool and urine.

text_flags.why: possible: 'neha' for meha (m/n confusion); meha fits the series of disorders

notes: Objects of 'hanyāt' in 34 (the long list runs 31-34). 'medas' as a condition probably means excess fat or obesity (probable); kept as 'fat'. The Sanskrit is a single compound ending in saṅgraham.

words.gloss: uneven, irregular; fever; irregular fever (viṣamajvara, intermittent fever; probable)

hindi: विषम ज्वर यानी अनियमित बुखार, विसर्प यानी फैलने वाली त्वचा की सूजन, एक अस्पष्ट शब्द जिसका अनुमानित पाठ ध्मान यानी अफारा है, आध्मान यानी अफारा और प्रवाहिका यानी मरोड़ के साथ दस्त।
english: Viṣamajvara (irregular fever), vīsarpa (spreading skin inflammation, erysipelas), an unclear word (on a conjectural reading dhmāna, flatulence), ādhmāna (bloating) and pravāhikā (dysentery with straining).

text_flags.why: possible: 'sarṣa' for sarpa (p/ṣ confusion); the final 'dhma' is probably dhmāna but this is not certain

notes: Continues 31 (objects of hanyāt in 34). The word 'dhma' is doubtful, so the translation of it is conjectural. Identifications: viṣamajvara = irregular or intermittent fever (probable); vīsarpa = erysipelas-like spreading inflammation (probable); pravāhikā = dysentery (probable).

words.gram: f. acc. pl.; the whole is dvandva ending in rujaḥ

hindi: कमर के जोड़ पर, जाँघ, कटि, कुक्षि, मन्या यानी गर्दन के पिछले भाग, कान और सिर की पीड़ाओं को।
english: The pains of the groin, thigh, waist, flank, nape of the neck, ear and head.

text_flags.why: possible: 'mandyā' is not a body part; 'manyā' (nape) fits the list of body parts

notes: Continues 31-32 (objects of hanyāt in 34). 'rujaḥ' ends the compound and governs all earlier members: 'pains of X, Y, ...'.

words.gloss: it would destroy, it may destroy
unclear (aśma 'stone'; kuṇḍala 'ring'; not a known disease name)
words.gram: m. acc. pl.; damaged or corrupt

hindi: यह असृग्दर यानी असामान्य मासिक रक्तस्राव, उन्माद, शोफ यानी सूजन, कास यानी खाँसी और अश्मकुण्डल को नष्ट करे, जो अस्पष्ट शब्द पर अनुमानित पाठ है।
english: It may destroy asṛgdara (abnormal menstrual bleeding), insanity (unmāda), swelling (śopha), cough (kāsa) and aśmakuṇḍala (an unclear word, on a conjectural reading).

text_flags.why: possible: 'aśma-kuṇḍala' is not a disease name; perhaps aśmarī (urinary stone) with a corrupt second part; kept unsplit and not interpreted

notes: Governs the objects listed in 31-33. Subject is the basti of 30. 'asṛgdara' = abnormal uterine bleeding (probable). The last word is doubtful and is not interpreted.

hindi: आँखों के लिए हितकर, पुत्र देने वाला, यापनों का राजा, रसायन।
english: Good for the eyes, giver of sons, the king of the yāpanas (sustaining enemas), a rejuvenative (rasāyana).
notes: Epithets of the basti of 30; no verb in the line.

words.gloss: separately; pala (a unit of weight); portion
words.gram: n. acc. sg., bahuvrīhi or adv.

words.gloss: without gokṣura (gokṣura, small caltrops, Tribulus terrestris; standard)

hindi: प्रत्येक को अलग-अलग एक पल के अंश में गोक्षुर के बिना पंचमूल को पकाए।
english: One should cook the pañcamūla (the five roots) without gokṣura (small caltrops), each separately in a portion of one pala.
notes: 'pṛthakpalāṃśam' is read as 'separately, in portions of a pala'. 'pañcamūlam agokṣuram' is the five-root group in which gokṣura is not included; which group is not stated here. gokṣura = Tribulus terrestris (standard).

hindi: एक आढक दूध में, चार प्रस्थ, पिसे हुए यष्टि आदि से युक्त।
english: In an āḍhaka of milk (a measure of volume), four prasthas (a measure of volume), joined with the ground (ones) beginning with licorice (yaṣṭi).
notes: Elliptic: the thing measured as 'four prasthas' is not named (the decoction of 36 carried over is the natural reading but not stated); no verb. 'yaṣṭyādi' = 'beginning with licorice'; the group is not listed here. Continues 36.

words.gloss: honey; oil; ghee; sindhūttha (born of Sindh, rock salt; standard); joined with

hindi: शहद, तैल, घी और सिन्धूत्थ यानी सैन्धव से युक्त बस्ति भलीभाँति प्रशंसित है।
english: The enema (basti), joined with honey, oil, ghee and sindhūttha (rock salt), is highly esteemed.
notes: 'su pūjitaḥ' is the printed spacing; read as supūjitaḥ 'well esteemed'. 'sindhūttha' = rock salt (standard).

words.gloss: child; old (person); woman; delicate (person); comfort; nature; comfort-natured

hindi: विशेष रूप से बच्चों, बूढ़ों, स्त्रियों, सुकुमारों और सुखी स्वभाव वालों के लिए।
english: Especially for children, the old, women, the delicate and those of a comfort-loving nature.
notes: No verb; continues 38 ('esteemed'). Printed 'vāla' is read as bāla (child; v/b orthographic normalisation). The genitive plural is rendered 'for'; 'sukhātman' is read as 'of comfortable nature' (comfort-loving).
